REPORT ON Japanese Intelligence.

Made by D.S. Kim Forwarded by Ruffo, a.a.C.P.

About 50 representatives of the Japanese Street Unions held a meeting at 7 p.m. May 16 in the Japanese Club, Boone R'd , on matters concerning the organization of the Japanese Reservists Association. It is reported that an urgent meeting of representatives

explained to the audience the duties of the reservists.

members of the association.

preparation to cope with the situation.

REPORT ON Japanese Intelligence.

Made by D. S. Kim Forwarded by R. Forke, A. C. I. P.

It is reported that the contents of the petition
telegraphed by the local Japanese Chamber of Commerce to the
Japanese Government yesterday are as follows:-

"Although anti-Japanese feeling is growing stronger
every day owing to the fabricated propaganda of Chinese
regarding the Tsinan affair, we are safe here at present
under the proper protection of our naval force. We
believe it will not be beneficial for Japanese should
further trouble spread along the Yangtsze Valley,
therefore, we are desirous that our government will
carefully consider the matter and take drastic action,
should Japanese life and property be threatened in
future."

D. S. Kim
D. S.

A meeting of the committees of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions, and Japanese Resident ' Association, was held at the Japanese Club, Boone Road, on May 9th when the following measures to be taken during a time of emergency were decided, and a Special Headquarters Committee appointed, as follows,

Mr. Otozaki - Vice Consul. Mr. Yonesato - Chairman of the Japanese Chamber of Commerce, Mr. Fukushima - member of S.M.C. Mr. Kawabata - Chairman of Committee of Japanese Residents' Corporation.

Sections. The Committee will decide
(1) when the Roads - North Szechuen Road and Northern District are safe.
(2) In case only the Settlement is safe.
(3) In case of danger in and to the Settlement.

(1) residents of District under their charge when necessary to evacuate, and shall consider other necessary measures to be taken. Mr. Hanasato, Chief of Police is in charge of this Section.

THE CANTON GAZETTE, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 22, 1928

THE BOYCOTT AS A WEAPON

People who are not accustomed to ponder well over all the phases of some given subject are usually in the habit of passing their judgment off hand. Thus it is that we often hear the remark made in certain quarters that the boycott is a cowardly weapon, the explanation offered for this sort of reasoning being that its enforcement is tantamount to "hitting below the belt." In Shanghai, in the "longest bar in the world," where queer theories are daily expounded between cocktails as to how best to "save China from her ills", the boycott is held up as a typical example of "John Chinaman's cowardly nature". Not so long ago, the present writer heard a "prominent" Shanghailander declare that he "had no use for a people who refused to go to war", which in his opinion is the "direct method" of dealing with opponents, but who nevertheless did not mind hitting the other fellow below the waist. Just why it is that some folks are in the habit of reasoning things out in this manner we are not in a position to say—but it is, however, true that all up and down the China Coast, where good fellows get together, this sort of reasoning is daily expounded.

The fact of the matter is that the boycott is not only not a cowardly way of bringing one's opponent to reason but is a courageous method of expressing resentment towards acts of wanton Imperialism. The present anti-Japanese boycott is not so much directed towards the Japanese people but the Tanaka Government which, from its very inception, sought to coerce China or a portion of it into becoming a vassal of Japan. What better reason is there for the Chinese people to refuse to continue to be treated to Big Stick policies than the dispatch of troops to China on the slightest pretexts ostensibly for the purpose of protecting Japanese lives and properties but in reality to indulge in land-grabbing and control of the country's economics? And what better method is there to bring it home to the Japanese nation that the Chinese people highly resent the Imperialistic tendencies of the Tanaka government? Wars never accomplish anything, they but cause the loss of innocent and valuable lives. Boycotts, on the other hand, give the other fellow ample time to think things over. Therefore, we say, the boycott, as a weapon, is much the more honorable.

There is a tendency now on the part of Japan's propagandists to minimize the serious consequences of the present boycott to the Japanese side. Mr. George Bronson Rea, chief exponent of the Japanese Cause now has an associate in the person of Mr. Sokolsky. Mr. Rea does not say very much these days but Mr. Sokolsky has been trying to make out that the loss of business by the Japanese in China as a result of the boycott is infinitesimal; that Japan's trade with the rest of the world has increased, and that the boycott will but incite the Japanese traders and manufacturers to greater efforts to sell Japanese products to other nations. This story sounds peculiarly similar to that of the fox and the grapes! Presumably Mr. Sokolsky does not understand Japanese. If he does, and if he would make it a point to HEAR what the Japanese traders in North and South China have to say in respect of the shortsightedness of the Tanaka government's China policy, Mr. Sokolsky would be in a better position to judge the real facts of the situation. But Mr. Sokolsky, like Mr. Rea, prefers to hear what the sabre-rattling Tokyo premier has to say. However, as they have it in French, CHACUN A SON GOUT.

《广州公报》，1928年11月22日，星期四

抵制作为武器

那些不习惯于仔细推敲某个特定主题各个方面的人，通常习惯于草率地做出判断。因此，我们经常听到某些方面的人说，抵制是一种懦弱的武器，对这种推理的解释是，执行抵制相当于“击打腰带以下部位”（即使用卑鄙手段）。在上海，在这个“世界上最长的酒吧”里，人们每天一边喝着鸡尾酒，一边阐述各种奇怪的理论，讨论如何最好地“将中国从苦难中拯救出来”，抵制被视为“中国人懦弱本性”的典型例子。不久前，笔者听到一位“著名”的上海老外人宣称，他“看不起拒绝参战的民族”，在他看来，这是对付对手的“直接方法”，但他却不介意击打对方的腰部以下。为什么有些人习惯于以这种方式进行推理，我们无从置喙——但确实，在整个中国沿海地区，每当好人聚在一起时，每天都会听到这种论调。

事实是，抵制不仅不是迫使对手讲理的懦弱方式，反而是表达对肆意帝国主义行为愤慨的勇敢方法。目前的反日抵制运动与其说是针对日本人民，不如说是针对田中内阁，该内阁自成立之初就试图胁迫中国或其部分地区成为日本的附庸。对于中国人民来说，拒绝继续忍受大棒政策还有什么比这更充分的理由呢？日本借口保护日本人的生命和财产，实则从事土地掠夺和控制该国经济，以此为由向中国派兵。还有什么比这更好的方法让日本国民明白，中国人民高度反感田中政府的帝国主义倾向呢？战争从来不能成就任何事业，只会造成无辜且宝贵的生命损失。另一方面，抵制给对手留出了充分的时间来反思。因此，我们要说，作为一种武器，抵制要光荣得多。

目前，日本的宣传人员有一种倾向，即淡化当前抵制运动对日本方面的严重后果。乔治·布朗森·雷亚（George Bronson Rea）先生是日本事业的主要代言人，现在他有一位名叫索科尔斯基（Sokolsky，音译）先生的同伴。雷亚先生最近话不多，但索科尔斯基先生一直试图表明，日本在华业务因抵制而遭受的损失微乎其微；日本与世界其他地区的贸易有所增加，而且抵制只会激励日本贸易商和制造商更加努力地向日益其他国家销售日本产品。这个故事听起来特别像狐狸和葡萄的故事！想必索科尔斯基先生不懂日语。如果他懂，并且如果他能留心倾听中国南北各地的日本贸易商对田中政府短视的对华政策的看法，索科尔斯基先生就能更好地判断局势的真实情况。但是，索科尔斯基先生和雷亚先生一样，更愿意听那位挥舞军刀的东京首相说什么。然而，正如法国人所说，各有所好（CHACUN A SON GOUT）。

THE CANTON GAZETTE, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 23rd 1928

THE EFFECTS OF THE BOYCOTT

In our issue of yesterday, we commented editorially upon the futility of minimizing the effects of the boycott. Mr. Sokolov had written that what Japan lost in China as a result of the movement was more than counter-acted by her trade expansion in other regions. This sort of reasoning is very poor consolation indeed to the multitude of Japanese small traders in China whose business has been well-nigh ruined by the boycott. One has only to hear the comments of the small Japanese traders in China to realize fully the seriousness of the situation in so far as these traders are concerned.

There are some 250,000 Japanese in Manchuria and 60,000 in the rest of China. Only a few Japanese concerns in China come under the category of large corporations. In fact, one can almost count such corporations on the fingers of one's hands. The vast majority of Japanese concerns in China is composed of one or two-men affairs, with a capital ranging from 10,000 yen to 50,000 yen. The large corporations, with ramifications in Japan and in countries other than China, are, of course, not so seriously affected by the boycott, but there is no question that the small concerns have their backs to the wall, and are seriously worrying over the coming year-end settlement.

If the boycott continues indefinitely, as the result of Baron Tanaka's sabre-rattling policy in China, what will be the final plight of these small traders? It may be true that Japan's trade with other countries has expanded to such an extent that the decline of Japanese trade in China does not affect Japanese finances, but can anyone truly affirm that this is of benefit to the small Japanese traders in China? If they finally become so reduced in circumstance as to be unable to carry on any longer, will the Japanese Government turn over the surplus accrued from Japan's trade with South America and India, say, to these small traders in China?

The plight of the Japanese traders in Manchuria is not as serious as that of those in the rest of China. But then, the average turn-over of the Japanese small trader in the Three Eastern Provinces is, in normal times, not as large as the turnover of his compatriot in other parts of the Chinese Republic. In South China, the Japanese small trader with a capital of 10,000 yen, has an annual turn-over of 40,000 yen in normal times, whereas in Manchuria, the average turn-over does not greatly exceed the capital involved. From this it will be seen how serious is the situation to the Japanese small traders in China.

As a result of the shortsighted policy of Baron Tanaka, whose conception of diplomacy is the free use of the Big Stick, the small Japanese traders in China are now holding goods which they are unable to sell. Nor are they able to enter into fresh commitments with Chinese merchants. Many not only owe money to the banks but to manufacturers and suppliers in Japan as well, and the coming year end will find these unfortunate people in dire straits.

It is all very well for the propagandists to paint rosy word pictures in an effort to hoodwink the general public, but the real facts belie all these pro-Tanaka effusions.

抵制的影响

在昨天的期刊中，我们发表了社论，评论了淡化抵制影响的徒劳无功。索科洛夫（Sokolov，音译）先生写道，日本因此次运动在中国遭受的损失，已被其在其他地区的贸易扩张所抵消。这种推理对于那些在华日本小商人来说确实是很糟糕的安慰，他们的生意几乎被抵制毁于一旦。人们只需听听在华日本小商人的评论，就能充分认识到就这些商人而言局势的严重性。

满洲约有25万日本人，中国其他地区有6万人。在华日本企业中，只有少数属于大公司类别。事实上，这样的大公司屈指可数。在华绝大多数日本企业是由一两人经营的小本生意，资本在1万日元至5万日元之间。当然，在日本和中国以外的国家设有分支机构的大型公司受抵制的影响不那么严重，但毫无疑问，小公司已陷入绝境，并正为即将到来的年终结算而严重担忧。

如果由于田中男爵在中国的挥舞军刀政策导致抵制无限期持续，这些小商人的最终困境会是什么？日本与其他国家的贸易扩大到如此程度，以至于对华贸易的下降不影响日本财政，这可能是真的，但谁能真正断言这对在华日本小商人有利呢？如果他们最终陷入如此困境而无法继续经营，日本政府会将例如从与南美洲和印度的贸易中获得的盈余转交给这些在华小商人吗？

满洲日本商人的困境不如中国其他地区的日本商人那样严重。但是，在正常时期，东三省日本小商人的平均营业额并不如中华共和国其他地区的同胞那么大。在华南，拥有1万日元资本的日本小商人在正常时期的年营业额为4万日元，而在满洲，平均营业额并没有大大超过所涉资本。由此可见，在华日本小商人的处境是多么严峻。

由于田中男爵短视的政策——他的外交理念就是随意使用大棒——在华日本小商人现在持有无法售出的货物。他们也无法与中国商人达成新的承诺。许多人不仅欠银行的钱，还欠日本制造商和供应商的钱，即将到来的年终将使这些不幸的人陷入绝境。

宣传人员为了蒙蔽公众而描绘美好的前景图画，这固然很好，但真实的事实驳斥了所有这些亲田中的溢美之词。

Comments.
1. As the British Consulate was outside the Japanese Defence Zone, it was not possible to get such good information or to witness the proceedings as effectively as if one had been inside that area.
2. The telephone system went out of order very shortly after the affair started and remained so during the whole period under review. Telegraphic communication also ceased from May 1st.
3. The origin of the conflict remains obscure, everybody appears to have a different version, varying in fact in proportion with their Chinese or Japanese sympathies. It is certain, however, that the Chinese made several attempts to force the Japanese sentries in the same manner as they have employed before. An eye-witness informed me of a coolie, who was observed to bare his breast and advance towards a sentry, daring him to strike. The sentry complied with his request? R.I.P.
4. The conduct of the Japanese soldiers has been admirable: they show an utter disregard of danger, and though they treat the Chinese in a distinctly harsh manner, it is only in accordance with their mode of training. Towards foreigners, they have observed a firm but respectful attitude.
Their morale is excellent.
5. The Chinese have also respected foreign property up to date, but even before the clash occurred, there were indications that this would not remain the case for long.
As soldiers, they cannot be considered as anything more than an armed rabble, their deficiencies being thrown into glaring relief by their contact with trained troops. Approximately 30,000 Chinese troops have been literally hunted out of TSINAN by 3,000 Japanese and a squad of Japanese soldiers is sufficient to set a whole Chinese battalion running. Their morale appears to be completely broken. How this army has fought its way up from CANTON, passes one's comprehension.
6. A most gratifying spectacle was afforded by the disarmed Southern troops, particularly the long-haired type of student-officer, whose shamed-faced attitude was a pleasant contrast to anything one has seen hitherto.
7. It was noticed that the Chinese grey uniforms were less conspicuous than the Japanese Khaki: the red ca-band and rank badges of the latter made a good target. The detachment which came from TIENTSIN wore tin helmets.
A few of the Chinese soldiers also had tin hats.
8. The Consular armament consists of six old type long Lee-Enfield rifles and some Mark VI ammunition of 1910 date. It is suggested that if this armament is really intended for use in emergency, a more modern type might be furnished.
9. In conclusion, it must be acknowledged that the Chinese have at last obtained what they have been asking for.
For the first time, within recent years they have encountered forcible opposition, and retribution has been meted out to them in a manner which might have been employed at HANKOW and NANKING. Subsequent events will prove the justification or otherwise of the Japanese action. Suffice it to say, for the moment, the Chinese have received the most salutary lesson since the Boxer rebellion.

评论。
1. 由于英国领事馆位于日本防区之外，因此无法像身处该区域内那样有效地获取如此优良的情报或目击事态进程。
2. 电话系统在事件发生后不久即发生故障，并在整个审查期间一直未能恢复。电报通信也自5月1日起中断。
3. 冲突的起因仍然不明，每个人似乎都有不同的说法，其事实差异程度与其亲华或亲日倾向成正比。然而可以肯定的是，中国人曾多次试图以他们以前使用过的同样方式强行突破日本哨兵。一名目击者告诉我，曾看到一名苦力袒露胸膛，向一名哨兵逼近，挑衅对方开枪。哨兵满足了他的要求？愿他安息（R.I.P.）。
4. 日本士兵的表现令人钦佩：他们表现出对危险的完全无视，虽然他们对待中国人的方式明显严厉，但这仅符合他们的训练模式。对外国人，他们保持着坚定但尊重的态度。
他们的士气极佳。
5. 迄今为止，中国人也尊重外国财产，但即使在冲突发生之前，就有迹象表明这种情况不会持续太久。
作为士兵，他们只能被视为一群武装暴民，其与受过训练的部队接触时，其缺陷暴露无遗。大约30,000名中国军队被3,000名日本人 literally（字面上/实际上）赶出了济南（TSINAN），一小队日本士兵就足以让整整一个中国营溃逃。他们的士气似乎已彻底崩溃。这支军队是如何从广州（CANTON）一路打上来的，实在令人费解。
6. 被解除武装的南方军队，特别是那种留长发的学生军官类型，呈现出一种极为令人欣慰的景象，他们羞愧的态度与迄今所见的一切形成了愉快的对比。
7. 人们注意到，中国军队的灰色制服不如日本的卡其色制服显眼：后者红色的领章和军衔徽章成为了很好的靶子。从天津（TIENTSIN）来的分队佩戴钢盔。
少数中国士兵也戴有钢盔。
8. 领事馆的武器装备包括六支旧式长李-恩菲尔德步枪和一些1910年生产的马克VI型弹药。建议如果这些装备确实旨在用于紧急情况，或许应提供更现代化的型号。
9. 总之，必须承认，中国人终于得到了他们一直要求的东西。
近年来，他们第一次遭遇了强力反对，并且受到了本可能在汉口（HANKOW）和南京（NANKING）采用的那种方式的报复。后续事件将证明日本行动的正当性与否。 suffice it to say（ suffice it to say /  suffice it to say），暂且可以说，中国人自义和团运动以来接受了最有益的一课。

May 5th. 1928.
On May 4th, the British Consul General had an interview with Chiang Kai-shek, in which the latter requested the good offices of the former to get into touch with the Japanese authorities with a view to ending hostilities. Owing to all communications being broken down, (the telephone ceased functioning an hour after the affair started) I took the message to the Japanese Consulate. The streets were still deserted and some action was going on down one of the streets as I passed. The part of the town near the Japanese Consulate appeared to have suffered severely in the fighting, several houses being wrecked and in some cases burnt out.
The following information was obtained from the Consul General:-
(i) The present activity was due to the clearing up of certain areas by the Japanese troops.
(ii) Gunmen and snipers were still very active and several bombs had been thrown at the troops from various points: one or two had exploded in the Consulate.
(iii) Japanese military casualties amounted to 17 killed and 40 wounded, a further seven were reported killed during the morning.
(iv) Communication with TSINGTAO was interrupted, the Kiaochow-Tsinan line was cut out in no fewer than eighteen places. The W/T plant which had been brought down from TIENTSIN would not function properly.
(v) He had been in touch with Chiang Kai-shek and the latter had promised to withdraw his troops from the Settlement, but apparently his orders could not, or would not be carried out.

After this interview, I visited the General Staff Headquarters which were now located in a house almost opposite the Japanese Consulate, where I met the G.O.C. (General Fukuda) and the Chief of Staff (Colonel Kuroda). They both corroborated the statements made by the Consul General and Colonel Kuroda expressed some apprehension as to the possible shortage of food supplies owing to the railway being cut.
I returned to the Consulate at 1215 hours.
No thing of interest occurred during the afternoon until 1700 hours, when a Company of Japanese infantry and a machine gun section proceeded to search the houses to the South of the Consulate. The object in view was to clear out the gunmen and also to search for any Japanese civilians who might be there. The plan was admirably carried out, the machine guns being placed at each corner in order to fire down either road, while the infantry, with some Chinese Police went through the buildings. Four Chinese were observed to be shot, and several shots in the buildings probably accounted for some more. The affair finished at about 1900 hours.
At 2030 hours, a Japanese armoured car came round with an official from the Japanese Consulate and the American Consul, with a request that we should accompany them to the Japanese lines to witness some corpses of Japanese civilians who had been caught by the Chinese soldiers. We proceeded to the Military Hospital. In the mortuary, a most unpleasant sight was revealed: twelve corpses were laid out, all more or less badly mutilated. Two of them were women, one an obviously young girl who had been dealt with in the typical Chinese manner. The corpses of several Japanese soldiers were also seen.
A further batch of infantry reinforcements, strength about 500 men, was seen to arrive about 2100 hours.
We returned to the Consulate in the armoured car at about 2230 hours.

1928年5月5日。
5月4日，英国总领事会见了蒋介石，后者请求前者斡旋，以便与日本当局取得联系，旨在结束敌对行动。由于所有通信线路中断（电话在事件发生一小时后停止运作），我将口信带至日本领事馆。街道依然空无一人，当我经过时，其中一条街道上正发生某些行动。日本领事馆附近的城区似乎在战斗中遭受了严重破坏，几所房屋被毁，有些甚至被烧毁。
从总领事处获得以下信息：-
(i) 目前的行动是由于日军正在清理某些区域。
(ii) 枪手和狙击手仍然非常活跃，并从各个地点向部队投掷了数枚炸弹：其中一两枚在领事馆内爆炸。
(iii) 日军伤亡人数为17人死亡，40人受伤，另有七人据报在上午期间死亡。
(iv) 与青岛（TSINGTAO）的通信中断，胶济铁路线至少有十八处被切断。从天津（TIENTSIN）运来的无线电台设备无法正常运作。
(v) 他已与蒋介石取得联系，后者承诺将其部队撤出租界，但显然他的命令未能或不愿被执行。

此次会面后，我访问了总司令部，该司令部现位于几乎正对日本领事馆的一所房屋内，在那里我会见了司令官（福田将军）和参谋长（黑田上校）。两人都证实了总领事的陈述，黑田上校对因铁路被切断可能导致的粮食供应短缺表示了一些担忧。
我于12时15分返回领事馆。
下午直至17时前未发生值得注意之事，此时一连日本步兵和一个机枪排开始搜查领事馆以南的房屋。其目的是清除枪手，并搜寻可能在那里的日本平民。该计划执行得非常出色，机枪部署在每个角落以封锁两条道路，而步兵则在一些中国警察的陪同下穿过建筑物。观察到四名中国人被枪击，建筑物内的几声枪响可能还造成了更多伤亡。事件大约在19时结束。
20时30分，一辆日本装甲车携同日本领事馆官员和美国领事前来，请求我们陪同他们前往日军防线，观看一些被中国士兵抓获的日本平民尸体。我们前往陆军医院。在停尸房，呈现出一幅极其令人不快的景象：十二具尸体陈列在此，均受到不同程度的严重残害。其中两名为女性，一名显然是年轻女孩，遭到了典型的中国式对待。还看到了几名日本士兵的尸体。
另一批约500人的步兵增援部队于21时左右抵达。
我们于22时30分左右乘装甲车返回领事馆。

December 8, 1928 THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW 53.

Boycott Seriously Affecting Japanese Traders in Both North and South China
BY J. A. J.

There is a tendency now on the part of Japan's propagandists to minimize the serious consequences of the present boycott to the Japanese side. Mr. George Bronson Rea, chief exponent of the Japanese Cause, has now an associate in the person of Mr. Sokolsky. This latter gentleman has been trying to make out that the loss of business by the Japanese in China as a result of the boycott is infinitesimal, that Japan's trade with the rest of the world has increased, and that the boycott will but incite the Japanese traders and manufacturers to greater efforts to sell Japanese products to other nations. This story sounds peculiarly similar to that of the fox and the grapes! Presumably Mr. Skolsky does not understand Japanese. If he does, and if he would make it a point to hear what the Japanese traders in North and South China have to say in respect of the shortsighted China policy of the Tanaka government, Mr. Sokolsky would be in a much better position to judge the real facts of the situation.

The fact of the matter is that the Japanese in China have been very seriously affected by the boycott. The big Japanese firms, in view of their business interests and connections in various parts of the world, and because of their ability to secure credits from the Japanese banks as well as assistance from the Japanese Government whenever needed, are, of course, in a position to more or less face periods of stress, but for every large Japanese concern in China there are a couple of hundred of small traders and it is these small traders that have been very seriously hit by the boycott. When it is taken into consideration that there are some 200,000 Japanese in Manchuria and 60,000 in the rest of China, one immediately realizes that the few large Japanese business houses in China do not represent the real standard of the effects of the anti-Japanese boycott. There are countless one-man concerns with capital ranging from 10,000 to 50,000 yen that are now faced with serious difficulties and the propagandists would do well to study their plight before indulging in silly attempts to minimize the real nature of the situation.

Japanese Traders Are Worried

The small Japanese traders in China, from Mukden to Canton, are worrying over the fast approach of the end of the year, the time to effect a settlement with their creditors, namely the manufacturers in Japan who have extended credit to them, and the banks who have granted them overdrafts. Their funds are all tied up in goods and these goods cannot be sold on account of the boycott. Of course conditions vary in the various parts of China, for example the small Japanese traders in Manchuria, while affected, are in a better position than the traders in the rest of China, but we must not run away with the idea that just because there are 200,000 Japanese in Manchuria and only 60,000 in the rest of China, the better situation of the former counteracts the predicament of the latter. Such is not at all the case. For the average Japanese small trader in Manchuria does not, in normal times, have anything approaching the turn-over of the average Japanese trader in Central or South China. Whereas the Mukden small trader, with a capital of 10,000 yen, may have a turn-over of 40,000 yen annually (in normal times), the Canton small trader, with a similar capital, may easily have an annual turn-over of 80,000 yen in normal times.

It is a poor way of reasoning that just because the trade of Japan with countries other than China has increased, whatever is lost in China is to be considered as infinitesimal. It may be some consolation to the Japanese manufacturers to be able to sell 25 per cent. more goods to South America and India, thereby off-setting the 25 per cent. lost in China, but it is poor consolation to the small Japanese traders in China. Napoleon referred to the English as being a "nation of shopkeepers" but these "shopkeepers" have kept the Union Jack flying. Just as the middle class is usually the backbone of a nation, the "small traders" are usually the backbone of trade. How many individuals are there who can set up a company with a capital of a million, a half million or even a quarter of a million dollars? Only a very few in comparison with the multitude of persons who are able to start business with a capital of a few thousand dollars.

Mr. Sokolsky does not seem to have taken the trouble to ascertain all the facts. What he has done is to swallow the doses given by headquarters! If Mr. Sokolsky knows Japanese and would investigate the predicament of the small Japanese traders in China, he would be a bit more wary of minimizing the effects of the anti-Japanese boycott. It is a poor method to take as a standard the expansion of Japan's trade with other countries in off-setting the decline of Japanese business in China. It is not only unscientific but too transparent. Such propaganda stunts do not really lead anywhere.

Indignant at Tanaka's Policy.

The small Japanese traders in China are justly indignant with Tanaka's China policy. They have seen how the Chinese have persistently refrained from purchasing Japanese products even though they may have been called upon to pay higher prices for goods from other countries. In piece goods, we have the authority of Japanese consular officials in South China for it that British goods have largely supplanted Japanese goods. The writer has compiled a list of goods hitherto largely imported from Japan but which are now entering China from other countries. The material for this article has been secured from a score of Japanese small traders in South China and not from Baron Tanaka, nor yet from Mr. Yamamoto of the South Manchuria Railway Company.

Cotton blankets hitherto entered China on a large scale from Japan. Now, they are imported from Great Britain and Germany, with a percentage from the United States. Piece goods are now largely brought from England and Germany. Perfumery and toilet articles now come almost solely from the United States, France and Germany. In Patent Medicines, there is a great decline in imports from Japan, hitherto a large supplier. In Sea Products, the Japanese trade has been lost in favor of Java, British India and to some extent the United States. In Paper, almost all of China's requirements are now filled by countries other than Japan.

To say that the small Japanese traders in China are highly dissatisfied with the China policy of the Tanaka government and greatly discouraged as to the future is putting it very mildly indeed. Many have lost every cent they have saved in the past several years from profits earned and are now carrying on in a hand-to-mouth manner. The plight of these small merchants is no joke although the propagandists have sought to make fun of the boycott and its consequences. In South China as well as in Central China many are facing bankruptcy, and unless the Japanese government finds the money to assist these small merchants to weather the storm, there is going to be great distress at the year end.

A Protest to Tokyo

It is reported that the small Japanese traders in South China are proposing to send delegates to Tokyo, not for the purpose of pressing for the maintenance of a firm "positive policy" towards China but for financial aid and for the introduction of a policy more in consonant with the times. These small merchants complain, not without reason, that they are innocent victims of the situation and that on account of the suberatting policy of the Tanaka Government, they are held up to objurgation by the Chinese. The impression of non-Japanese is that all Japanese are blindly patriotic and at all times make it a point to stick to their Government through thick and thin. This may be true of the Meiji era but is certainly far from being the case now.

It is a well known fact that Japanese consular officials in China have reported fully upon the plight of the small traders in this country, pointing out the danger of "dangerous thoughts spreading among them. While no one has been heard to say anything against the Emperor, many have expressed the desire to see Baron Tanaka consigned to Hades. Paper dealers, piece-goods merchants, dealers in toys and perfumery and toilet articles are one and all in serious straits.

Japan may be making the extra 25 per cent elsewhere to counter-balance the 25 per cent. of her foreign trade lost in China but that is not helping the small traders in this country in any way.

The writer explained to a Japanese trader the other day the substance of Mr. Sokolsky's recent propaganda article. The trader promptly replied that the Japanese Government has got together a number of foreigners for its tools. The Japanese Government, he said, is always very clever that way!

Canton, Dec. 2, 1928.

1928年12月8日 《密勒氏评论报》 第53页。

抵制运动严重影响了华北和华南的日本商人
作者：J. A. J.

目前，日本的宣传人员有一种倾向，即淡化当前抵制运动对日本方面造成的严重后果。作为“日本事业”的主要代言人，乔治·布朗森·雷亚（George Bronson Rea）先生现在有一位同伴，即索科尔斯基（Sokolsky）先生。这位先生一直试图表明，日本人在华因抵制而遭受的商业损失微乎其微，日本与世界其他地区的贸易有所增长，且抵制只会激励日本商人和制造商更加努力地将其产品销往其他国家。这种说法听起来特别像狐狸与葡萄的故事！想必索科尔斯基先生不懂日语。如果他懂，并且肯花点心思去听听华北和华南的日本商人对于田中内阁短视的对华政策有何看法，那么索科尔斯基先生在判断局势的真实情况时，处境会好得多。

事实是，在华日本人受到抵制运动的严重影响。大型日本公司鉴于其在全球各地的商业利益和联系，并且因为它们在需要时能够从日本银行获得信贷以及从日本政府获得援助，当然有能力或多或少地应对困难时期；但是，在华每一家大型日本企业背后，都有数百家小商贩，正是这些小商贩受到了抵制运动的沉重打击。考虑到满洲约有20万日本人，中国其他地区有6万日本人，人们立刻就会意识到，在华少数大型日本商号并不能代表反日抵制运动影响的真实水平。无数资本在1万至5万日元之间的单人商行正面临严重困难，宣传人员在沉溺于淡化局势真实性质的愚蠢尝试之前，最好先研究一下他们的困境。

日本商人忧心忡忡

从奉天到广州，在华的日本小商贩们都在为年底的迅速临近而担忧，这是他们与债权人——即向他们提供信贷的日本制造商以及给予他们透支额度的银行——进行结算的时候。他们的资金全部积压在货物上，而这些货物因抵制运动而无法售出。当然，中国各地的情况各不相同，例如，满洲的日本小商贩虽然受到影响，但处境比中国其他地区的商人要好；但我们不能想当然地认为，仅仅因为满洲有20万日本人，而中国其他地区只有6万人，前者的较好状况就能抵消后者的困境。事实绝非如此。因为在正常时期，满洲普通日本小商贩的营业额远不及华中或华南普通日本商人的营业额。例如，拥有1万日元资本的奉天小商贩，（在正常时期）年营业额可能为4万日元；而拥有同等资本的广州小商贩，在正常时期的年营业额很容易达到8万日元。

仅仅因为日本与非中国国家的贸易增加，就认为在中国失去的份额微乎其微，这是一种糟糕的推理方式。日本制造商能够将更多25%的商品销往南美洲和印度，从而抵消在中国损失的25%，这对他们来说或许是一种安慰，但对于在华的日本小商贩来说，这种安慰微不足道。拿破仑曾称英国人为“店主的民族”，但这些“店主”却让米字旗高高飘扬。正如中产阶级通常是一个国家的脊梁，“小商贩”通常是贸易的脊梁。有多少人能够设立资本为一百万、五十万甚至二十五万美元的公司？与那些能够以几千美元资本起步创业的大多数人相比，这样的人寥寥无几。

索科尔斯基先生似乎并未费心去查明所有事实。他所做的只是吞下了总部给出的药方！如果索科尔斯基先生懂日语，并愿意调查在华日本小商贩的困境，他在淡化反日抵制运动的影响时会更加谨慎。以日本与其他国家贸易的扩张作为标准，来抵消日本在华业务的下滑，这是一种拙劣的方法。这不仅不科学，而且过于露骨。此类宣传伎俩实际上毫无用处。

对田中政策感到愤慨。

在华日本小商贩对田中的对华政策感到正当的愤怒。他们看到，中国人坚持不购买日本产品，即使这意味着他们不得不以更高的价格购买其他国家的商品。在匹头布料方面，我们有日本驻华南领事官员的权威说法，证实英国商品已很大程度上取代了日本商品。笔者编制了一份清单，列出了迄今为止主要从日本进口、但现在从其他国家进入中国的商品。本文的材料取自华南的二十名日本小商贩，而非来自田中男爵或南满洲铁道公司的山本先生。

棉毯以前大量从日本进入中国。现在，它们从英国和德国进口，另有部分来自美国。匹头布料现在主要从英国和德国运入。香水和化妆用品现在几乎完全来自美国、法国和德国。在专利药品方面，从日本——迄今的主要供应国——的进口大幅下降。在海产品方面，日本的贸易份额已丧失，转而 favoring 爪哇、英属印度，以及在一定程度上是美国。在纸张方面，中国的需求现在几乎全部由日本以外的国家满足。

说在华日本小商贩对田中政府的对华政策极为不满，并对未来深感沮丧，这话说得还算是非常含蓄的。许多人失去了过去几年从利润中积攒的每一分钱，现在只能勉强维持生计。尽管宣传人员试图嘲笑抵制运动及其后果，但这些小商人的困境绝非儿戏。在华南以及华中，许多人正面临破产，除非日本政府拿出资金帮助这些小商人渡过难关，否则年底将出现巨大的困苦。

向东京抗议

据报道，华南的日本小商贩正提议派遣代表前往东京，其目的并非为了敦促维持对华强硬的“积极政策”，而是为了寻求财政援助，并引入更符合时代潮流的政策。这些小商贩抱怨说——这种抱怨不无道理——他们是局势的无辜受害者，并且由于田中政府的煽动性政策，他们成为了中国人谴责的对象。非日本人的印象是，所有日本人都盲目爱国，并且始终坚持以无论顺境逆境都支持其政府为原则。这在明治时代或许属实，但现在肯定远非如此。

众所周知的事实是，日本驻华商事官员已充分报告了该国小商贩的困境，指出“危险思想”在他们中间蔓延的危险。虽然没人听到有人说过反对天皇的话，但许多人都表示希望看到田中男爵下地狱。纸商、匹头布料商、玩具商以及香水和化妆用品商全都陷入严重困境。

日本可能在其他地方赚取额外的25%以平衡其在中国损失的那25%对外贸易，但这对本国的小商贩没有任何帮助。

前几天，笔者向一名日本商人解释了索科尔斯基先生最近那篇宣传文章的要点。该商人立即回答说，日本政府召集了一些外国人作为其工具。他说，日本政府在这方面总是很狡猾！
